title: Proxyless image provisioning + operator quarantine: acceptance criteria and handshake for isolated VPCs
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Problem: Some customers deploy Redwood Private into environments that cannot allow outbound HTTP(s) to public registries or to Redwood-owned proxies. We need a clearly scoped PRD defining a proxyless image provisioning flow and an operator quarantine/handshake protocol so on-prem operators can safely bootstrap, validate, and upgrade runtime images and operators without egress. This ticket captures requirements, trade-offs, acceptance criteria, and operational runbook artifacts required for sign-off.
background: Customers: regulated finance and government customers with strict egress policies or physically air-gapped datacenters.

Current state: Private package bootstrap assumes outbound access to Redwood mirror endpoints or customer-configured proxy; offline-only flows currently rely on manual ingestion guidance that lacks automated validation and safe rollback semantics.

Goal: Provide an automated, auditable, and minimal-trust operator handshake that enables image provisioning (OCI/manifest-based), signature verification, and quarantined operator activation, while preserving an offline upgrade path and clear rollback criteria.
acceptance_criteria: Artifact ingestion: Customers can push signed OCI image tarballs or an index manifest to a customer-controlled internal registry or object store and trigger an automated verification job locally with no outbound egress required.
Signature verification: Runtime verifies image signatures against a customer-provisioned root-of-trust (KMS/HSM or uploaded public keys). Verification must be enforced before any operator activation.

Operator quarantine: New operator images are staged in a quarantined namespace and cannot be scheduled onto production nodepools until a multi-step handshake completes (validation tests pass, digital signature verified, and operator-level small-canary applied to a dedicated test namespace).

Deterministic rollback: If a canary or validation job fails, the operator is prevented from rolling out; a documented rollback (automatic or one-click manual) must revert to the previously active operator image and KV cache migration must be reversible within the SLO window.

Offline upgrade playbook: Provide a runbook that includes checksum reconciliation steps, KMS key rotation guidance for offline keys, and physical media ingestion procedures for customers that accept removable-media artifact transfer.

Telemetry constraints: Telemetry emitted during ingestion/handshake must be configurable to zero egress; if telemetry is enabled it must respect customer allowlists and be redactable. Default for air-gapped installs is telemetry off.
Audit logs: All handshake steps, signature checks, and operator lifecycle events must be recorded locally and accessible via the Console API for at least 90 days (configurable).

Test harness: An automated test harness (runnable offline) that simulates a corrupted manifest, expired signature, and successful canary must exist; results are captured as pass/fail artifacts linked to the runbook.
non_goals: Building a fully managed public mirror service for air-gapped customers (we will provide tooling and operators to use customer registries or physical media).
Replacing customer-side artifact signing policies or KMS choices; we provide integration points and sample configs.
tradeoffs_and_risks: Strict enforcement of signature verification increases time to bootstrap; provide an escape hatch for an emergency signed-authority, gated by SRE approval and audit logs.
Fully offline verification requires customers to manage keys (KMS/HSM) — operational burden is shifted to customers but reduces trust surface for Redwood.
Quarantine and canary mechanisms add complexity to operator lifecycle; must balance UX for small teams vs. safety for regulated orgs.
decisions: Adopt OCI index + detached signatures (cosign) as the canonical artifact format for offline ingestion (keeps compatibility with common registries).
Support two trust models: customer-managed public keys (uploaded) and KMS-wrapped keys (customer HSM/KMS). Redwood will not hold private signing keys for air-gapped installs.
Default behavior for Private installs is telemetry=off; enabling telemetry requires explicit local operator consent and allowlist configuration.
implementation_notes: Components: ingestion CLI (offline), local verification service (in-cluster, runs as a Job), quarantine controller (operator extension), canary runner (CRD for small workloads).
Operator changes: add image staging controller, signature validation hook, and a quarantine admission controller that blocks scheduling until handshake completes.
UX: Console flow for 'ingest artifact' that generates a local checklist and a signed verification receipt customers can store offline.
Backward compatibility: Provide toggles to opt out of quarantine for non-regulated customers, but keep signature verification recommended for all installs.
testing_plan: Unit tests for signature verification code paths including key parsing and rejection of invalid signatures.
Integration: offline ingestion end-to-end using local registry (Harbor/Artifactory) and simulated HSM (soft KMS).
Chaos: simulate partial network availability during ingestion and ensure deterministic rollback and operator remains in quarantined state on failure.
Acceptance: Security review and internal red-team validation of the operator handshake.
progress_updates: 2025-03-01: Ticket created after discovery call with a regulated-banking pilot customer (notes linked).
2025-03-02: Spike completed — validated cosign workflow works with on-prem Harbor; prototype ingestion CLI v0.1 created (github.com/redwood/infr/PR-4122).
2025-03-04: Architecture review with Infra and Security: agreed on quarantine admission controller; Security requested formal threat model and key-rotation guidance.
2025-03-05: Draft runbook uploaded to Drive (drive.google.com/drive/folders/1ExampleStub) and assigned to Solutions Eng for pilot packaging.
next_steps: Produce a short threat model and circulate to Security by 2025-03-10.
Finish the offline test harness and attach CI jobs that can run entirely in local k8s by 2025-03-18.
Schedule pilot with banking customer and Solutions Eng to validate runbook and signing workflow in April.
